source_text: CAPUT VICESIMUM QUARTUM, De creatione in genere. Hucusque vidimus de DEO, hominis omniumque rerum principe ac rege, quantum ad essentiam et subsistentiam suam, qua illius sufficientia continetur, tanquam primario Christianae religionis objecto, tum quae natura ejus seu qualis sit Deus, tum quis sit, seu cur haec natura tribuenda sit, ne summo vero Deo aliquid tribuatur inconveniens, neve alius aut alienus DEUS pro vero illo ac summo habeatur: sequuntur efficientiae illius, tanquam causae, ob quas Deo religio debetur, creatio nimirum et hominis instauratio. Christi et religionis Christianae necessitas pendet et elucet potissimum ex his duabus causis, propter quas Deus jus habet eam ab hominibus postulandi, tum ut creator, tum ut salvator in Filio dilectionis suae, sub quo etiam continetur, quod velit esse glorificator.
english: CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR. On creation in general.

Thus far we have seen concerning GOD, prince and king of man and of all things, as to His essence and subsistence, by which His sufficiency is contained, as the primary object of Christian religion — both what His nature is or what sort God is, and who He is, or why this nature is to be attributed, lest something unsuitable be attributed to the highest true God, or another or alien GOD be held for that true and highest: there follow His efficiencies, as causes on account of which religion is owed to God, namely creation and the restoration of man.

The necessity of Christ and of Christian religion hangs and shines chiefly from these two causes, on account of which God has the right of demanding it from men — both as creator and as savior in the Son of His love, under which is also contained that He wills to be glorifier.

source_text: Prolixe quidem et erudite hic inseruntur vulgo dogmata de divinis decretis et consiliis, quorum consideratio, ut ardua et abstrusa est, ita a posteriori suis locis omnium optime et tutissime suscipietur: ne ecclesias Germanicas satis jam diu divulsas periculosis altercationibus de praedestinatione, reprobatione, providentia magis atque magis divellamus, atque dilaceremus, ut annis aliquot praeteritis in vicino nobis Belgio, pro dolor, accidit. Sobrie vero et magna cum religione, sine scrupulositate, de consiliis et viis Domini cogitandum et loquendum est nobis — Isa. LV; Rom. XI.33-34. Nihil hic caro et sanguis potest, sed omnia ex Apocalypsi Patris caelestis petenda sunt, quae Gen. I.1 Deus in principio et ante omnia patefecit per actum CREATIONIS horum caelorum et hujus terrae, quae certe revelatio revelationum est, et virtute sua omnes reliquas complectitur. Hoc est alphabetum omnis notionis et actionis.
english: At length indeed and learnedly there are commonly inserted here dogmas concerning divine decrees and counsels, whose consideration, as it is hard and abstruse, so will be undertaken most well and safely of all a posteriori in their own places: lest we tear and lacerate still more the German churches already long enough divided by dangerous altercations concerning predestination, reprobation, providence, as some years past happened, alas, in neighboring Belgium.

But soberly and with great religion, without scrupulosity, we must think and speak concerning the Lords counsels and ways — Isaiah 55; Romans 11:33-34. Nothing here can flesh and blood, but all things are to be sought from the heavenly Fathers Apocalypse, which Genesis 1:1 God in the beginning and before all things made known through the act of CREATION of these heavens and this earth, which certainly is the revelation of revelations, and by its power embraces all the rest. This is the alphabet of every notion and action.

source_text: II. Creatio vero consideranda est tum in se, tum in ordine ad creaturas. III. In se considerata creatio est actio Dei, qua Deus Pater per Filium in Spiritu sancto ex nihilo produxit caelum et terram et omnia quae in eis sunt — Gen. I.1; Psal. XXXIII.9; Hebr. XI.3; Apoc. IV.11. Creatio est productio rei ex nihilo sui et subjecti, sive, ut loquuntur, ex non ente negativo et privativo. Ideoque est aliquid medium inter id quod est facere, et inter illud quod est impedire ne quis faciat, quando de permissione loquimur; at creatio proprie est effectiva impletio decreti per voluntatem et potentiam Dei.
english: II. But creation is to be considered both in itself and in order to creatures. III. Creation considered in itself is Gods action by which God the Father through the Son in the Holy Spirit produced from nothing heaven and earth and all things that are in them — Genesis 1:1; Psalm 33:9; Hebrews 11:3; Revelation 4:11.

Creation is production of a thing from nothing of itself and of subject, or, as they say, from negative and privative non-being. And therefore, when we speak of permission, there is something middle between doing and hindering lest someone do; but creation properly is the effective fulfilling of the decree through Gods will and power.

source_text: IV. Estque immediata aut mediata. Immediata est, qua Deus sine medio creaturae, solo nutu voluntatis, res producit — ut caelum et terra in principio, angeli, anima rationalis. VI. Mediata est, qua res e principiis jam creatis, Deo tamen primario agente, producuntur — ut plantae, animalia e terra et aquis diebus sequentibus. VII. Exsistentia vero rerum mediate creatarum non minus a Deo pendet quam immediate creatarum; Deus enim in omnibus operatur.
english: IV. And it is immediate or mediate. Immediate is that by which God without a creatures medium, by the sole nod of will, produces things — as heaven and earth in the beginning, angels, the rational soul.
VI. Mediate is that by which things are produced from principles already created, God yet primarily acting — as plants, animals from earth and waters on the following days.
VII. But the existence of things mediately created hangs no less from God than of those immediately created; for God works in all things.

source_text: XIII. Neque tantum est rerum omnium efficienter creatio a solo Deo, sed et nulla creatura creare potest. XIV. Impellens vero creationis causa est bonitas Dei communicativa, seu amor quo Deus bonum suum ad extra communicare voluit. Materia proprie dicta rebus creatis non praejacuit; creatio enim est ex nihilo. Qui materiam aeternam fingunt cum Aristotele, aut duas principia cum Manichaeis, a veritate aberrant.
english: XIII. Nor is creation of all things efficiently from God alone only, but also no creature can create. XIV. But the impulsive cause of creation is Gods communicative goodness, or the love by which God willed to communicate His good outwardly.

Matter properly so called did not lie beforehand for created things; for creation is from nothing. Those who invent eternal matter with Aristotle, or two principles with the Manichees, wander from the truth.

source_text: XXVII. Forma creationis est ipse divinus jussus seu fiat — Psal. XXXIII.9; II Pet.? Ex quo Deus FONS appellatur. XVIII. Finalis causa creationis est gloria Dei, et bonum creaturarum subordinatum gloriae Dei — Prov. XVI.4; Rom. XI.36; Apoc. IV.11. XX. Rerum inaequalitas non est a materia, sed a Dei sapientissima ordinatione, ut sit ordo et harmonia in universo. XXII. Atque haec de creatione communiter: sequentur creaturae, quae spectantur vel conjunctim, vel discretim. Conjunctim spectatae MUNDI nomine veniunt: discretim appellantur opera tum principii, tum primae noctis, tum sex dierum. CAPUT VICESIMUM QUINTUM, De mundo, sequitur.
english: XXVII. The form of creation is the divine command itself or fiat — Psalm 33:9. From which God is called FOUNTAIN. XVIII. The final cause of creation is Gods glory, and the good of creatures subordinated to Gods glory — Proverbs 16:4; Romans 11:36; Revelation 4:11.
XX. Inequality of things is not from matter but from Gods most wise ordination, that there may be order and harmony in the universe.

XXII. And these things concerning creation commonly: there will follow creatures, which are regarded either jointly or discretely. Regarded jointly they come under the name WORLD: discretely they are called the works of the beginning, of the first night, and of the six days. CHAPTER TWENTY-FIVE, On the world, follows.
